results.title: Strategy-specific evidence, coverage gaps and adverse-news exits
results.text: C2 always checks dated evidence before a permitted action. For a code-qualified strong EMA_TREND or confirmed EMA_PULLBACK entry (ADX at least 22, Close above EMA20 above EMA50) or RSI_REVERSION (RSI below 42, Close above 0.88 EMA50), missing financial or independent news coverage alone is not an entry veto. Inspect company evidence and attempt bounded dated web retrieval when coverage is missing or unknown. With no identified concrete unresolved adverse event, a LIMITED assessment may use COVERAGE_LIMITED, an observed attempted WEBSCAN or ready official SCAN citation, empty event_risks and explicit coverage limitations. This permits following the technical signal with residual evidence risk; it never establishes clean fundamentals, safety or profit. Concrete potentially serious unresolved event risk remains UNKNOWN and blocks entry; it cannot be hidden as a mere coverage gap. A ready supported scan with no adverse finding can use NO_MATERIAL_ADVERSE_FOUND. BREAKOUT (including BREAKOUT_BOUNCE) entry requires readable dated corroborating company evidence, exact document citations, breakout_support explaining the source-backed support, and a supported adverse assessment. COVERAGE_LIMITED cannot justify breakout. Actual cited adverse news uses REVIEW_REQUIRED with ADVERSE_EVENT_FOUND or MATERIAL_ADVERSE and nonempty supported event_risks. Both adverse categories block entry; in a holding review they require EXIT after independent critic verification. A genuine adverse event, not a negative keyword, is necessary. A routine penalty or notice that is not material under POL-MAT-01 is a limitation, not an adverse event. Routine trading-window closure for insiders is not business closure or proof of insider wrongdoing. Interpret substantive disclosure_context and exact source windows; do not treat address fragments as monetary exposure. Attribute issuer-reported Nil and preserve missing impact as unknown. Market and critic independently read the current hashed company pack and observed policy evidence. Daily bounded official issuer metadata checks can trigger holding research between scheduled reviews; empty checks make no generation call. Publication and availability must be at or before the historical cutoff; after-close releases are first considered at a later eligible close. A confirmed exit queues a later-open simulated sale, with existing gap/stop/profit protections; no same-close look-ahead and no forced end-period liquidation. Stops, fees, position sizing, Friday/gap refresh, human approval where required and execution remain code controlled. Search failures and truncated sources are recorded; a live dated web lookup is not a certified historical content archive or exhaustive news feed. Lessons cannot override this policy or the independent critic. Breakout corroboration must be structured as document_id, kind, exact contiguous visible quote and relevance, with source availability no more than 30 calendar days before the signal cutoff. Code checks a reported benefit metric and an earnings/operating improvement or completed commercial event; prose alone, an auditor review, vague business focus, provider selection or a prospective forecast is insufficient. Sole support consisting of plans, expected/indicated gains or up-to targets is not an achieved result. The independent critic must separately quote and corroborate the same source; accept=true alone is insufficient. A structurally valid source and critic approval still do not predict price direction. Known recent explicit structural-action disclosures also invoke the raw-price entry quarantine in POL-60. Reject unsupported quotes rather than invent missing evidence; later profit or loss must never select a historical entry.

results.title: Breakout regime precedence
results.text: BREAKOUT requires Close above Prior20High and ADX14 at least 18, after high-volatility rejection. Prior20High is the maximum high over the prior 20 sessions, excluding the current session. This breakout classification is evaluated before the TREND classification and permits the BREAKOUT strategy.

results.title: Trend regime classification
results.text: TREND requires ADX14 at least 22 and EMA20 above EMA50, after higher-priority warm-up, high-volatility and breakout checks. Code permits EMA_TREND for this regime. A permitted route is distinct from an entry signal and does not guarantee an executable or profitable order.

results.title: Trend score evidence
results.text: For a trend candidate, strength combines 60 percent of ADX14 divided by 40, capped at one, and 40 percent of positive 20-session momentum divided by 0.10, capped at one. This intermediate strength is then used in the common stock-selection score; it is not a probability of profit.

results.title: EMA trend exit
results.text: The EMA_TREND signal exit is EMA20 below EMA50. The historical engine queues that exit for a subsequent eligible open and also applies protective-stop logic. A model explanation cannot modify the moving-average windows or submit an unapproved external-style exit.

results.title: Breakout strategy entry and exit
results.text: BREAKOUT enters on a ready row when Close exceeds the shifted prior 20-session high and ADX14 is at least 18. Its signal exit is Close below EMA20. The current high is not included in Prior20High, preventing a same-session high from entering its own comparison window. Breakout uses separately configured risk (default 0.5% equity), initial stop 2.5 ATR, trailing 2.5 entry ATR activated after 1R close gain. Stop fills first. One later confirmed re-entry per setup is allowed within ten trading sessions: close above stopped level, EMA20 and previous high; ADX>=18; no high-vol or warmup. Fresh C2 and the same strict recent source quote and independent critic are mandatory. Fill at a later eligible open. No same-candle rebuy or averaging down. A second stop exhausts the setup; profit/adverse exits do not create rebound watches. The approved catalogue includes EMA_PULLBACK for PULLBACK: ADX14>=22, EMA20>EMA50, an EMA20 touch holding EMA50 in a prior three-session window, followed by a completed close above EMA20 and prior-session high. Exit on EMA20<EMA50, or code protective/profit/C2 exits. Routing gives this confirmed pullback priority over breakout. BREAKOUT_BOUNCE is portfolio-owned stop/rebound context and routes only to BREAKOUT.

results.title: EMA trend exit

results.title: Strategy-specific evidence, coverage gaps and adverse-news exits
results.text: C2 always checks dated evidence before a permitted action. For a code-qualified strong EMA_TREND or confirmed EMA_PULLBACK entry (ADX at least 22, Close above EMA20 above EMA50) or RSI_REVERSION (RSI below 42, Close above 0.88 EMA50), missing financial or independent news coverage alone is not an entry veto. Inspect company evidence and attempt bounded dated web retrieval when coverage is missing or unknown. With no identified concrete unresolved adverse event, a LIMITED assessment may use COVERAGE_LIMITED, an observed attempted WEBSCAN or ready official SCAN citation, empty event_risks and explicit coverage limitations. This permits following the technical signal with residual evidence risk; it never establishes clean fundamentals, safety or profit. Concrete potentially serious unresolved event risk remains UNKNOWN and blocks entry; it cannot be hidden as a mere coverage gap. A ready supported scan with no adverse finding can use NO_MATERIAL_ADVERSE_FOUND. BREAKOUT (including BREAKOUT_BOUNCE) entry requires readable dated corroborating company evidence, exact document citations, breakout_support explaining the source-backed support, and a supported adverse assessment. COVERAGE_LIMITED cannot justify breakout. Actual cited adverse news uses REVIEW_REQUIRED with ADVERSE_EVENT_FOUND or MATERIAL_ADVERSE and nonempty supported event_risks. Both adverse categories block entry; in a holding review they require EXIT after independent critic verification. A genuine adverse event, not a negative keyword, is necessary. A routine penalty or notice that is not material under POL-MAT-01 is a limitation, not an adverse event. Routine trading-window closure for insiders is not business closure or proof of insider wrongdoing. Interpret substantive disclosure_context and exact source windows; do not treat address fragments as monetary exposure. Attribute issuer-reported Nil and preserve missing impact as unknown. Market and critic independently read the current hashed company pack and observed policy evidence. Daily bounded official issuer metadata checks can trigger holding research between scheduled reviews; empty checks make no generation call. Publication and availability must be at or before the historical cutoff; after-close releases are first considered at a later eligible close. A confirmed exit queues a later-open simulated sale, with existing gap/stop/profit protections; no same-close look-ahead and no forced end-period liquidation. Stops, fees, position sizing, Friday/gap refresh, human approval where required and execution remain code controlled. Search failures and truncated sources are recorded; a live dated web lookup is not a certified historical content archive or exhaustive news feed. Lessons cannot override this policy or the independent critic. Breakout corroboration must be structured as document_id, kind, exact contiguous visible quote and relevance, with source availability no more than 30 calendar days before the signal cutoff. Code checks a reported benefit metric and an earnings/operating improvement or completed commercial event; prose alone, an auditor review, vague business focus, provider selection or a prospective forecast is insufficient. Sole support consisting of plans, expected/indicated gains or up-to targets is not an achieved result. The independent critic must separately quote and corroborate the same source; accept=true alone is insufficient. A structurally valid source and critic approval still do not predict price direction. Known recent explicit structural-action disclosures also invoke the raw-price entry quarantine in POL-60. Reject unsupported quotes rather than invent missing evidence; later profit or loss must never select a historical entry.

results.title: Breakout regime precedence
results.text: BREAKOUT requires Close above Prior20High and ADX14 at least 18, after high-volatility rejection. Prior20High is the maximum high over the prior 20 sessions, excluding the current session. This breakout classification is evaluated before the TREND classification and permits the BREAKOUT strategy.

results.title: Trend regime classification
results.text: TREND requires ADX14 at least 22 and EMA20 above EMA50, after higher-priority warm-up, high-volatility and breakout checks. Code permits EMA_TREND for this regime. A permitted route is distinct from an entry signal and does not guarantee an executable or profitable order.

results.title: Trend score evidence
results.text: For a trend candidate, strength combines 60 percent of ADX14 divided by 40, capped at one, and 40 percent of positive 20-session momentum divided by 0.10, capped at one. This intermediate strength is then used in the common stock-selection score; it is not a probability of profit.

results.title: EMA trend exit
results.text: The EMA_TREND signal exit is EMA20 below EMA50. The historical engine queues that exit for a subsequent eligible open and also applies protective-stop logic. A model explanation cannot modify the moving-average windows or submit an unapproved external-style exit.

dated 23•• August 2023, the Company has received an order dated 22•• August 2023 from

Details desired under relevant provisions of Regulation 30 are given as under:

adverse_scan.scope: Bounded official NSE issuer-disclosure metadata search plus readable matched attachments; not exhaustive press or proof of no adverse information.

web_scan.scope: Two bounded financial/adverse queries; up to four trusted source pages. Not exhaustive web/news coverage or proof of safety. Publication metadata is not a certified historical content-version chain.

data.constraint: Code-defined research route; entry signal and risk checks remain separate.

results.title: Strategy-specific evidence, coverage gaps and adverse-news exits
results.text: C2 always checks dated evidence before a permitted action. For a code-qualified strong EMA_TREND or confirmed EMA_PULLBACK entry (ADX at least 22, Close above EMA20 above EMA50) or RSI_REVERSION (RSI below 42, Close above 0.88 EMA50), missing financial or independent news coverage alone is not an entry veto. Inspect company evidence and attempt bounded dated web retrieval when coverage is missing or unknown. With no identified concrete unresolved adverse event, a LIMITED assessment may use COVERAGE_LIMITED, an observed attempted WEBSCAN or ready official SCAN citation, empty event_risks and explicit coverage limitations. This permits following the technical signal with residual evidence risk; it never establishes clean fundamentals, safety or profit. Concrete potentially serious unresolved event risk remains UNKNOWN and blocks entry; it cannot be hidden as a mere coverage gap. A ready supported scan with no adverse finding can use NO_MATERIAL_ADVERSE_FOUND. BREAKOUT (including BREAKOUT_BOUNCE) entry requires readable dated corroborating company evidence, exact document citations, breakout_support explaining the source-backed support, and a supported adverse assessment. COVERAGE_LIMITED cannot justify breakout. Actual cited adverse news uses REVIEW_REQUIRED with ADVERSE_EVENT_FOUND or MATERIAL_ADVERSE and nonempty supported event_risks. Both adverse categories block entry; in a holding review they require EXIT after independent critic verification. A genuine adverse event, not a negative keyword, is necessary. A routine penalty or notice that is not material under POL-MAT-01 is a limitation, not an adverse event. Routine trading-window closure for insiders is not business closure or proof of insider wrongdoing. Interpret substantive disclosure_context and exact source windows; do not treat address fragments as monetary exposure. Attribute issuer-reported Nil and preserve missing impact as unknown. Market and critic independently read the current hashed company pack and observed policy evidence. Daily bounded official issuer metadata checks can trigger holding research between scheduled reviews; empty checks make no generation call. Publication and availability must be at or before the historical cutoff; after-close releases are first considered at a later eligible close. A confirmed exit queues a later-open simulated sale, with existing gap/stop/profit protections; no same-close look-ahead and no forced end-period liquidation. Stops, fees, position sizing, Friday/gap refresh, human approval where required and execution remain code controlled. Search failures and truncated sources are recorded; a live dated web lookup is not a certified historical content archive or exhaustive news feed. Lessons cannot override this policy or the independent critic. Breakout corroboration must be structured as document_id, kind, exact contiguous visible quote and relevance, with source availability no more than 30 calendar days before the signal cutoff. Code checks a reported benefit metric and an earnings/operating improvement or completed commercial event; prose alone, an auditor review, vague business focus, provider selection or a prospective forecast is insufficient. Sole support consisting of plans, expected/indicated gains or up-to targets is not an achieved result. The independent critic must separately quote and corroborate the same source; accept=true alone is insufficient. A structurally valid source and critic approval still do not predict price direction. Known recent explicit structural-action disclosures also invoke the raw-price entry quarantine in POL-60. Reject unsupported quotes rather than invent missing evidence; later profit or loss must never select a historical entry.

results.title: RSI reversion exit threshold
results.text: RSI_REVERSION has a signal exit when RSI14 exceeds 58; the protective stop can exit earlier in historical replay. RSI identifies a configured setup rather than proof that an oversold stock must rebound. All stop, quantity and cash calculations remain deterministic.

results.title: Trend regime classification
results.text: TREND requires ADX14 at least 22 and EMA20 above EMA50, after higher-priority warm-up, high-volatility and breakout checks. Code permits EMA_TREND for this regime. A permitted route is distinct from an entry signal and does not guarantee an executable or profitable order.

results.title: RSI selection strength
results.text: For an RSI_REVERSION candidate, the intermediate strength is the value of (42 minus RSI14) divided by 22, clipped between zero and one. This measures depth relative to the project entry threshold after eligibility screening. It does not change the stop, cash or planned-risk controls.

results.title: Breakout strategy entry and exit
results.text: BREAKOUT enters on a ready row when Close exceeds the shifted prior 20-session high and ADX14 is at least 18. Its signal exit is Close below EMA20. The current high is not included in Prior20High, preventing a same-session high from entering its own comparison window. Breakout uses separately configured risk (default 0.5% equity), initial stop 2.5 ATR, trailing 2.5 entry ATR activated after 1R close gain. Stop fills first. One later confirmed re-entry per setup is allowed within ten trading sessions: close above stopped level, EMA20 and previous high; ADX>=18; no high-vol or warmup. results.title: Strategy-specific evidence, coverage gaps and adverse-news exits
results.text: C2 always checks dated evidence before a permitted action. For a code-qualified strong EMA_TREND or confirmed EMA_PULLBACK entry (ADX at least 22, Close above EMA20 above EMA50) or RSI_REVERSION (RSI below 42, Close above 0.88 EMA50), missing financial or independent news coverage alone is not an entry veto. Inspect company evidence and attempt bounded dated web retrieval when coverage is missing or unknown. With no identified concrete unresolved adverse event, a LIMITED assessment may use COVERAGE_LIMITED, an observed attempted WEBSCAN or ready official SCAN citation, empty event_risks and explicit coverage limitations. This permits following the technical signal with residual evidence risk; it never establishes clean fundamentals, safety or profit. Concrete potentially serious unresolved event risk remains UNKNOWN and blocks entry; it cannot be hidden as a mere coverage gap. A ready supported scan with no adverse finding can use NO_MATERIAL_ADVERSE_FOUND. BREAKOUT (including BREAKOUT_BOUNCE) entry requires readable dated corroborating company evidence, exact document citations, breakout_support explaining the source-backed support, and a supported adverse assessment. COVERAGE_LIMITED cannot justify breakout. Actual cited adverse news uses REVIEW_REQUIRED with ADVERSE_EVENT_FOUND or MATERIAL_ADVERSE and nonempty supported event_risks. Both adverse categories block entry; in a holding review they require EXIT after independent critic verification. A genuine adverse event, not a negative keyword, is necessary. A routine penalty or notice that is not material under POL-MAT-01 is a limitation, not an adverse event. Routine trading-window closure for insiders is not business closure or proof of insider wrongdoing. Interpret substantive disclosure_context and exact source windows; do not treat address fragments as monetary exposure. Attribute issuer-reported Nil and preserve missing impact as unknown. Market and critic independently read the current hashed company pack and observed policy evidence. Daily bounded official issuer metadata checks can trigger holding research between scheduled reviews; empty checks make no generation call. Publication and availability must be at or before the historical cutoff; after-close releases are first considered at a later eligible close. A confirmed exit queues a later-open simulated sale, with existing gap/stop/profit protections; no same-close look-ahead and no forced end-period liquidation. Stops, fees, position sizing, Friday/gap refresh, human approval where required and execution remain code controlled. Search failures and truncated sources are recorded; a live dated web lookup is not a certified historical content archive or exhaustive news feed. Lessons cannot override this policy or the independent critic. Breakout corroboration must be structured as document_id, kind, exact contiguous visible quote and relevance, with source availability no more than 30 calendar days before the signal cutoff. Code checks a reported benefit metric and an earnings/operating improvement or completed commercial event; prose alone, an auditor review, vague business focus, provider selection or a prospective forecast is insufficient. Sole support consisting of plans, expected/indicated gains or up-to targets is not an achieved result. The independent critic must separately quote and corroborate the same source; accept=true alone is insufficient. A structurally valid source and critic approval still do not predict price direction. Known recent explicit structural-action disclosures also invoke the raw-price entry quarantine in POL-60. Reject unsupported quotes rather than invent missing evidence; later profit or loss must never select a historical entry.

results.title: Breakout strategy entry and exit
results.text: BREAKOUT enters on a ready row when Close exceeds the shifted prior 20-session high and ADX14 is at least 18. Its signal exit is Close below EMA20. The current high is not included in Prior20High, preventing a same-session high from entering its own comparison window. Breakout uses separately configured risk (default 0.5% equity), initial stop 2.5 ATR, trailing 2.5 entry ATR activated after 1R close gain. Stop fills first. One later confirmed re-entry per setup is allowed within ten trading sessions: close above stopped level, EMA20 and previous high; ADX>=18; no high-vol or warmup. Fresh C2 and the same strict recent source quote and independent critic are mandatory. Fill at a later eligible open. No same-candle rebuy or averaging down. A second stop exhausts the setup; profit/adverse exits do not create rebound watches.
